description: Maps ATT&CK technique IDs to CyberSleuth threat categories, used to derive training labels from technique-labelled CTI sentences. Sub-techniques inherit their parent (T1566.001 -> T1566). A technique may map to several categories. Sentences whose techniques map to no category are labelled 'other'. Mappings are heuristics chosen by the project author, with the rationale recorded here; they are not part of ATT&CK.

phishing.rationale: Phishing (initial access) and Phishing for Information (reconnaissance).

ransomware.rationale: Data Encrypted for Impact is the defining ransomware behaviour. Inhibit System Recovery (shadow-copy deletion, etc.) is a strong ransomware precursor but also occurs in wipers, so this category can include some destructive non-ransomware activity.

vulnerability_exploitation.rationale: Every ATT&CK technique whose definition is exploitation of a software vulnerability, across tactics.

credential_theft.rationale: Core Credential Access techniques that obtain secrets. T1212 (Exploitation for Credential Access) maps to both this category and vulnerability_exploitation.

data_breach.rationale: All techniques of the ATT&CK Exfiltration tactic (TA0010) in v20.1: data leaving the victim environment.

ddos.rationale: Network and Endpoint Denial of Service. Too rare in procedure examples to train a model on (see dataset card); handled by the rule baseline.

not_derivable.malware: Almost every ATT&CK procedure example describes malware or actor behaviour, so 'malware' cannot be derived from a sentence's technique label. Handled by the rule baseline at report level.
